newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scandal-hit French cancer research chief hits back.
newsitem.headline: Scandal-hit French cancer research chief hits back.

text.p: The former head of France's leading cancer research association denied knowing anything about alleged fraud on Thursday, saying money he had received was payment for testing treatments for hair-loss and male impotence.
Jacques Crozemarie, 71, former president of the Association for Cancer Research (ARC) was released on bail last month pending possible trial after six months in detention.

He was forced to resign a year ago after state auditors found the ARC spent little more than 27.2 percent of its funds, or 124 million francs ($24 million), on research aid in 1993 while its top officials lived in grand style.

"I have told the investigating magistrate that any fraud, which has yet to be proven, happened behind my back...I have formally denied being aware of anything at all," Crozemarie told the newspaper Le Parisien.

Asked about allegations he was paid two million francs ($400,000) via an American company, Crozemarie said he had been manipulated and that the sum rewarded studies into hair-loss and male impotence which he had carried out using himself as a guinea-pig.
"I worked a lot on these two subjects which could lead to colossal fortunes... If my studies were found today, people would realise the quality of my work," Crozemarie said.

ARC's new chairman Michel Lucas has confirmed police reports that ousted officials swindled private donors of hundreds of millions of francs (tens of millions of dollars) through a system of fund transfers and false invoices.
Donations to charities tumbled amid a public outcry. A judge is formally probing eight other people on suspicion of fraud, forgery and misuse of corporate funds.
